questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The french system was not very user friendly but with help we managed to figure it out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My landlord took me to the apartment. At the UNi we had a welcome meeting

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have been better signs and waypoints

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Found it through the Danish church in Paris

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the distance and where other people live

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing facilitated through the Uni was not good

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Needed to get a student ID before being able to login and see relevant information. Not optimal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could write a message to the coordinators

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, I got the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: French administration is not the most helpful in the world

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was a lot lower than at Copenhagen University. It was all about memorizing what the professor had said at the lecture - no books. Exams were written in hand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was a lot lower than at Copenhagen University. It was all about memorizing what the professor had said at the lecture - no books. Exams were written in hand.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was not very engaging and it was a lot of one way communication. Not oriented against learning how to USE the law.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Business Law
IP Law
Criminal Law
Intro to British Law
Rules of Evidence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
IP law was rather okay despite it needing some more hours to dive into the subjects.
Rules of evidence was relevant but the exam was a "remember irrelevant stuff"-thing and should have been made to fit 2024

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Drinks are quite expensive and you spend a lot of money on food etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Possible to eat out at restaurants for less than in Copenhagen but bars etc were the same prices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really seem like there was a lot. Maybe I just didn't discover it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seemed like none. Language school but you could only attend if you could take ALL classes. I had some of the language classes overlap with my law courses and they wouldn't let me attend just some of the language classes and not all

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If possible, sports, I missed that

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out, do sports, see the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Rather easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: French people are not the most openminded so it takes a lot if you want to bond with them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Connecting with the french people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the appreciation of going out for dinner etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do not do it for the academic purpose - the uni is not at high level academically 
2) Do not live in Cergy, it is not a nice city - I lived in Pairs and took the train (RER A)
3) Find friends and be openminded

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: All the english exams are kind of on top of eachother - I had five exams within a week and 3 within 24 hours - it was awful!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the social experiences

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period was tough since I had so many exams on top of each other. Also you have to force yourself to meet people, I lived alone and because of that I didn't "automatically" meet a lot of people. But the people I became friends with were wonderful

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
